questions.q: Sorting sys.dm_exec_requests by cpu_time or logical_reads accomplishes what?
options: It surfaces the currently running request consuming the most CPU or I/O
It shows queries in the order they were originally written
It lists every historical query ever run on the instance
It ranks databases by size, not queries by cost
questions.explain: cpu_time and logical_reads are cumulative for the request so far, so sorting by them ranks active requests by resource consumption.

options: It's a DMF that turns a sql_handle into the actual, readable T-SQL text of the batch
It returns the list of all tables referenced by a stored procedure
It permanently logs every query executed on the server
It rewrites a query into a more efficient form automatically
questions.explain: sys.dm_exec_sql_text() is a Dynamic Management Function that resolves a sql_handle into query text.

questions.q: Why is CROSS APPLY used to combine sys.dm_exec_requests with sys.dm_exec_sql_text() and sys.dm_exec_query_plan()?
options: CROSS APPLY calls the table-valued function once per row of the DMV, passing that row's handle as the parameter
CROSS APPLY is required for any query involving more than one table
CROSS APPLY guarantees the query runs faster than a regular JOIN in all cases
CROSS APPLY is only valid syntax for catalog views, not DMVs
questions.explain: CROSS APPLY is the standard pattern for invoking a DMF once per row of a DMV, feeding it that row's handle (sql_handle or plan_handle).

questions.q: What does a non-zero blocking_session_id on a row in sys.dm_exec_requests indicate?
options: That request is currently blocked, waiting on another session
The request has finished executing successfully
The request is running under the sa login
The request's query plan has expired from cache
questions.explain: blocking_session_id identifies the session_id of the session blocking this request; zero means it isn't blocked.

questions.q: What format does sys.dm_exec_query_plan() return the execution plan in?
options: XML, which SSMS can open as a graphical execution plan
A plain-text summary with no visual representation
A CSV file listing each operator
A binary format only readable by DBCC commands
questions.explain: query_plan is returned as XML; clicking the result in SSMS renders it as the familiar graphical execution plan.
